about: Asset pipeline for the CQS reboot orbital fleet. All ship meshes, their textures and the tiling PBR materials are generated with fal.ai (fal MCP connector). three.js then plays Blender's role: import, orient, scale to game data, material upgrade, lighting and rendering. Designs are original; no legacy art is used as input.
style: Photorealistic spacecraft in a credible near-future 'naval-industrial' design language, as in a high-end aerospace concept photograph: faceted hard-surface hull with chamfered edges and layered armour plates, off-white thermal-control paint with realistic weathering, scuffs and panel-to-panel colour variation, signal-orange hazard and identification markings and stencilled hull numbers like on real naval ships, small cobalt-blue identification bands, bare brushed-metal and gunmetal structural frames, gold and silver multi-layer insulation blankets on sensor and electronics boxes, dark ceramic heat tiles on the belly, radiator panels, RCS thruster quads, antennas and hand rails at human scale, large fusion-drive engine bells with magnetic-nozzle coils, heavy radiation shielding between the drive and the crew sections. Physically based materials, real-world engineering logic, no aerodynamic wings, no neon, no glowing trim, not a video game, not stylised, not a toy. Original design, not based on any existing franchise.

bible.prompt: A professional concept art design sheet for an original science-fiction space fleet on a clean neutral light-grey studio background. Five ship classes arranged in a tidy grid, each large enough to read its details (not to scale), each with a small clean sans-serif caption: FIGHTER (compact single-seat space-superiority strike craft about 16 m long with a bubble canopy, a boarding ladder and access hatches, twin engines and forked stabiliser blades carrying cannons), CORVETTE (short, wide armoured escort gunship about 31 m long with two dorsal twin-barrel turrets, bow torpedo tubes, outrigger engine pods, a row of small bridge windows and crew airlock hatches), CIVIL FREIGHTER (long lean spine ship about 50 m long with a forward crew module with small windows and a docking hatch, a truss keel carrying stacked colourful cargo containers in orange, cobalt, teal, yellow and crimson, and an aft reactor and engine block), DESTROYER (long heavy warship about 67 m long with a blunt, faceted, armoured bow block, squared-off and not pointed, housing the recessed muzzle of a spinal mass-driver, three turrets, a stepped command tower with rows of small windows, big radiator panels and a cluster of engines, tiny hatches and ladders showing its size), FLEET CARRIER (huge slab-sided carrier about 260 m long with a wide open hangar bay in the bow lit by interior floodlights with tiny parked craft and deck crew visible for scale, a command island offset to one side with many rows of small windows, dark unlit matte-grey warp-field emitter vanes made of ribbed metal and ceramic with exposed cabling and mounting brackets, point-defence turrets and a massive engine cluster). Photorealistic spacecraft in a credible near-future 'naval-industrial' design language, as in a high-end aerospace concept photograph: faceted hard-surface hull with chamfered edges and layered armour plates, off-white thermal-control paint with realistic weathering, scuffs and panel-to-panel colour variation, signal-orange hazard and identification markings and stencilled hull numbers like on real naval ships, small painted cobalt-blue identification bands, bare brushed-metal and gunmetal structural frames, gold and silver multi-layer insulation blankets on sensor and electronics boxes, dark ceramic heat tiles on the belly, radiator panels, RCS thruster quads, antennas and hand rails at human scale, hatches, ladders and small windows that make each ship read as a real engineered object at its true size, large fusion-drive engine bells with magnetic-nozzle coils, heavy radiation shielding between the drive and the crew sections. Physically based materials, real-world engineering logic, no aerodynamic wings, no neon, no glowing trim, no glowing panel lines, no emissive strips, engines and emitters switched off, not a video game, not stylised, not a toy. Original design, not based on any existing franchise. Photorealistic, like a professional studio photograph of highly detailed physical models, soft even studio lighting, three-quarter views, natural materials and wear.
bible.note: 2 candidates judged by a 3-agent panel (originality, realism, consistency); candidate 0 chosen. The panel flagged the fighter as reading like a franchise fighter, so the fighter was redesigned (ships.fighter below) and generated with the approved corvette as an extra family reference.

A_concept.isolatedTemplate: Using the attached concept sheet only as the design-language reference, render ONLY the {class} as one isolated object: {description} Three-quarter view from the front-left and slightly above (camera about 35 degrees off the bow, 20 degrees up). The entire ship is visible and centred with generous empty margin, filling about 70% of the frame. Plain seamless light-grey studio background, soft even lighting, no floor, no cast shadow, no environment, no stars, no text, no labels, no engine exhaust plumes, no motion blur. Photorealistic, like a studio photograph of a highly detailed physical model with real materials and subtle weathering, sharp focus, suitable for 3D reconstruction. {style}

ships.fighter: a 16 m single-seat space-superiority fighter with a compact, non-aerodynamic layout: one elongated faceted armoured fuselage shaped like a flattened hexagonal pod, a small framed cockpit canopy set low and flush into the upper forward hull (not a bubble on a stalk), a heavy armoured engine block at the stern with two large fusion engine bells side by side, a dorsal spine carrying two short trapezoidal radiator panels laid flat along the hull, two compact weapon sponsons hugging the lower flanks each carrying a single long railgun barrel that runs forward alongside the nose, small missile bays with hatch doors on the belly, RCS thruster quads on the four corners of the hull, a sensor blister under the nose. No wings, no wingtip guns, no tail fins, no S-foils, nothing projecting outward from the sides. Bone-white thermal paint with signal-orange squadron bands, a small cobalt identification band and stencilled hull number F-402.
ships.corvette: a 32 m armoured escort corvette gunship: short, wide wedge hull, stepped bridge with a window band, two dorsal twin-barrel railgun turrets, four bow torpedo tube doors, two outrigger engine pods on armoured pylons, radiator panels, a sensor mast with gold-foil boxes, hull number K-214 in orange.
ships.freighter: a 50 m civil freighter: long lean spine ship with a compact forward crew module with windows, a boxed truss keel carrying two rows of stacked standard cargo containers in signal orange, cobalt, teal, sun-yellow, crimson and white, an aft shielded reactor module with radiators and two engines, teal civilian stripe and registry number CT-4.
ships.destroyer: a 68 m heavy destroyer: long armoured hull with a blunt faceted armoured bow block (not a triangular wedge) housing a large spinal mass-driver muzzle, three dorsal gun turrets with long barrels, a stepped command tower with a window band, sensor masts, big radiator panels along the flanks, a heavy engine block with four large plasma nozzles, hull number DD-12 in orange.
ships.carrier: a 260 m fleet carrier: huge slab-sided armoured hull with a wide open brightly lit hangar bay mouth in the bow showing a deck inside, a command island superstructure offset to the starboard side, dark metallic, unlit warp-field emitter vanes along the flanks, point-defence turrets, radiator arrays, a massive engine cluster of six nozzles at the stern, hull number CV-50 in orange.
ships.freighter-troops: a 50 m civil troop transport, the passenger variant of the same freighter family: identical compact forward crew module with windows, the same boxed truss keel, aft shielded reactor module, radiators and two engines, but instead of cargo containers the keel carries a row of three long pressurised cylindrical troop habitat modules, off-white with rows of small round windows, boarding hatches, docking collars and hand rails, teal civilian stripe and registry number CT-7.

D_materials.use: hull/orange/armor as tri-planar detail layers on the generated meshes; all sets as full materials for scene-built parts (hangar deck, engine bells, scale-lineup props)

D_materials_v2.params: same as D_materials (square_hd, all five maps, upscale_factor 2, tiling_mode both, png)
D_materials_v2.why: v8 look-dev: the hulls read as clean CG (uniform albedo, one dull matte sheen on every plate, no micro-surface, parts without contact shadow). Opt-in behind ?finish=worn (src/lib/finish.js) and ?ao=1 until the defaults are flipped.

hullWear.use: macro albedo tone (+-7.5 % per scale at one sigma, clamped +-20 %) and roughness breakup (0.55-0.95, mean 0.78) read tri-planar in the ship frame at ~46 m and ~190 m tiles (axes swapped between scales)

hullGrit.use: 0.8 m micro-surface: normal faded in only where a tile spans >= 40-220 px (no aliasing), roughness breakup at every distance

sootStreak.use: breakup of the drive soot stain round each bell lip (engines from the ship module)

D_materials_v2.runtime: each set ships a packed pack.webp (hullWear/sootStreak: z-normalised luminance, warm-cool chroma, soft luminance; hullGrit: normal xy + roughness) listed as runtimeMaps; manifest load:'finish' keeps them from loading unless the finish is on. The sets are deliberately low-contrast and PATINA's roughness/height for them came back flat (height a synthetic dither grid), so roughness is driven from the chroma and soft-luminance fields instead.
D_materials_v2.screenAO: three GTAOPass computed before the main render (lit opaque meshes only) and applied inside MeshStandard/Physical materials: indirect light fully, direct light 45 %; radius 2.5 % of the camera distance (1.5-14 m); off on the phone tier.
D_materials_v2.lighting: reviewed, unchanged: one hard sun, PMREM planet-shine at albedo 0.3 (shadow sides ~40 % of the lit side in sRGB, as in orbital photography with a sunlit planet below), exposure 1.7.
D_materials_v2.cost: 3 PATINA jobs, about $0.35 (list price $0.01 per megapixel; the first build's 11 sets were about $1.20)

realism: Futuristic but physically believable, never a cheap video-game look: real aerospace/naval engineering proportions and function, physically based materials (weathered white thermal paint, brushed and anodised aluminium, titanium, carbon composite, gold and silver MLI blankets, ceramic tiles), fine wear and grime, no neon trim, no glowing panel lines, no toy/cartoon/stylised shapes. Propulsion is fusion torch drives: large magnetic-nozzle engine bells whose exhaust is an intensely bright, long, blue-white plasma plume with faint shock diamonds; the plume is rendered in-scene, so 3D-reconstruction images show the engines unlit. Lighting reads like real photography: one hard sun, deep shadows, planet-shine, bloom only from genuinely bright sources.

v5_detail.why: Small details must be crisp and at true human scale for the ships' size to read: crew doors 2 x 1 m, ~1 m windows in rows one ~3 m deck apart, 1 m rails, 20-ft ISO containers.

method.fighter/corvette/destroyer/freighter fam: fal-ai/nano-banana-pro/edit of the approved v4 concept (4K, prompts name each oversized element; the fighter needed 'remove the canopy, plate it over, add a strip of small windows'; civil ships used crop-and-blend edits of the crew module), then a 4K turnaround, tripo3d/h3.1/multiview-to-3d (detailed geometry and texture), ingest (fighter/corvette textures now 4096) and a hull-number re-projection where the mesh garbled it (DD-12, CT-7).
method.carrier: nano-banana drew ~4 m windows at 900 m scale, so three fal-ai/patina/material tiles (flank ports, island ribbon panes, 2.7 m deck plating) sized from measured pixels are baked into an 8192 base-colour and normal texture by a texel-to-world lookup (dominant-axis projection per facet); geometry, UVs, hangar cavity and drive bells unchanged.

v5_detail.measured: bridge panes 0.5-0.8 m, ports 0.65-0.95 m, rails 1-1.8 m, hull numbers 2.2-2.3 m (carrier 15 m); still over target: some crew doors 3-4 m (destroyer flank boat hatch 5 x 9.5 m), civil containers ~1.5x ISO.

v6_repair.what: Texture-only repair of details the image model would not shrink: oversized crew doors repainted as plating + a 1.0 x 2.0 m door (fal-ai/nano-banana-pro door and boat-hatch decals, projected texel -> world -> view with a depth test); civil container stacks baked with two fal-ai/patina/material container tiles at true ISO size; corvette bridge emblem that read like a national flag painted out; opt-in magenta livery band for the civil ships.

v7_remodel.what: Every hull rebuilt as clean parametric hard-surface geometry in headless Blender (bpy 5.0) with the fal/Tripo mesh as the blueprint; small parts from two kits (assets/parts: fal nano-banana-pro + Tripo H3.1, 24 parts; assets/parts-blender: procedural, 31 parts) assembled by tools/blender/assemble.py. See README 'Remodel (v7)' and tools/blender/hulls/README*.md.
